title: Stoker metadata — shared definitions
description: Types every document of the metadata repository uses. Not a document of its own. Enum values are camelCase names, never the numbers the database stores: a public format outlives the order of a C# enum.

schemaVersion.description: `<major>.<minor>`: the version of the format a document was written for. A minor version only adds — fields, enum values, kinds — and never changes what an existing field means, so a reader of an older minor reads a newer document of the same major. It ignores fields it does not know, and a value it does not know in a field that only describes (a provider, a tag kind, a definition's origin) it treats as absent; an entry for a platform it does not know is not for this host. Something it does not know that would change what is done to an install — a fix role, a step kind, an integration provider or action — it never skips silently: it treats that build as needing a newer Stoker. A reader refuses a major it does not know.

uuid.description: A UUID in its lowercase hyphenated form. Ids are minted once, by whoever first adds the thing to the repository, and never change: a rename keeps the id.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the bytes, lowercase hex.

blake3.description: BLAKE3-256 of the bytes, lowercase hex.

relativePath.description: A path inside an install, relative to its root, with forward slashes. No leading slash or `~`, no backslash, no `:` (a drive, or an NTFS stream), no control character, no empty, `.` or `..` segment: the same rule the launcher applies before it touches a player's disk.

fileName.description: A bare file name: no slashes, no `:`, no control character, not `.` or `..`.

expandedString.description: A string the installing machine fills in. `%INSTALLDIR%` becomes the install's root folder, in the machine's own form (`C:\Games\Example` on Windows, `/home/me/Games/Example` elsewhere), without a trailing separator; `%%` is a literal `%`. Any other `%` is refused, so a value copied from somewhere with a placeholder of its own (`%APPDATA%`, `50%`) fails here rather than reaching a player's machine unexpanded.

launchKey.description: A launch by its key — stable where its display name is not: names get translated and reworded. One key may stand for a launch on each platform (`play` on Windows and on Linux).

languageTag.description: A BCP 47 language tag in its canonical casing — language, optional script, optional region: `en`, `de`, `pt-BR`, `zh-Hans`, `es-419`. One spelling per language, so `pt-BR` and `pt-br` are never two keys of one text. Stores name languages their own way (Steam's `english`, GOG's `en-US`); the exporter maps them, so a reader never has to know any store's list.

localizedText.description: One text in one or more languages, keyed by language tag. Plain text, paragraphs separated by a blank line; no HTML. Most entries hold `en` alone because that is what the stores were asked for — more languages are additions, not a different shape.

partialDate.description: A date as precisely as it is known: `2017`, `2017-02`, `2017-02-24`. Stores publish bare years and months, and padding them to the first of January would invent a fact.

provider.description: Where something came from: a store, or a database about games. `eshop` is Nintendo's (via titledb), `community` a contributor's own work.

source.description: Provenance: which provider a value was read from, and where. Kept so a value can be fetched again and checked, never to be served to players.

retrieved.description: The day it was read. A day, not a timestamp, so re-reading an unchanged value the same day is no diff.

definitionOrigin.description: Where an achievement, stat or leaderboard definition came from. `observed`: Stoker saw a running game use it and nobody has described it since — worth finding and completing. `curated`: written by a contributor.

platform.description: One operating system or console. The desktop and mobile systems run a build directly; every other value is a console, run through an emulator.

architecture.description: The instruction set a build's binaries are for. `any` is the honest answer when nothing determined it.

runtimeKey.description: A shared runtime by its stable key — `vcredist-14-x64`, `directx-jun2010`. Runtimes are described once, in the repository's own catalogue, never per game.

pluginKey.description: A plugin's identity: the reverse-DNS id its manifest declares (`org.example.filename-redirect`), or for a .NET assembly its name in lower case (`steamless.variant31.x64`, `sharpdisasm`).

pluginVersion.description: Three or four numbers, optionally a pre-release suffix: `1.2.0`, `3.1.0.5`, `0.0.0-legacy`. No build metadata (`+…`), because a version is also a file name.

pluginRef.description: A plugin of the plugin catalogue (`https://schemas.stokerhq.app/plugins/v1/`) — a hook plugin, a mod loader, a mod, an unpacker — pinned to one version. Pinned, because a newer version must never change what an existing entry installs. By key and version only, never by where the catalogue is kept, so the catalogue can live in a repository of its own.

downloads.description: Where the file's publisher offers it, in order of preference. Never a copy somebody else made: the repository redistributes nobody's binaries. Whatever comes back is checked against the file's hash, which alone decides whether it is the file; when every link is dead, an administrator supplies the file by hand and the hash still decides.

archive.description: When the URL serves an archive the file is inside: its format and the file's path in it.

pluginAssignment.description: A plugin applied to a game, or to one of its releases.

enabled.description: False only on a release: switches off the game's assignment of the same plugin for that release.

config.description: The plugin's options, checked against the configuration contract its manifest declares.

image.description: An image, inlined. The bytes are in the document, so a clone of the repository is the complete record — no CDN that a delisting can take down. `sha256` is of the decoded bytes, so a reader can check them and an instance can store each image once.

data.description: The image file, base64 (RFC 4648, padded, no line breaks).

contentFingerprint.description: What a set of files is, independent of where it is stored. An instance computes it from its own manifest and finds a repository build by it, so one entry describes the same files wherever they were ingested. The files themselves are never in the repository.

algorithm.description: `stoker-tree-1`: BLAKE3-256 over the UTF-8 text made of one line per file — `<path>\t<size>\t<blake3>\n`, path relative and forward-slashed, size in decimal bytes, the file's BLAKE3 in lowercase hex — ordered by path, ordinal. Empty directories do not count. The per-file BLAKE3 is the one every Stoker manifest already holds.

marker.description: One file that identifies a build even when the copy around it has changed. A copy a player had on disk has written its configs, saves and logs into the folder, or has a patch applied, so its fingerprint matches nothing; its executables and main data files usually still do. BLAKE3, because every Stoker manifest already holds it per file.

fileCheck.description: One file of an install as it has to be: there with these bytes, or not there at all.

fixCondition.description: What a copy has to be for a statement about it to hold. Every part has to: each file as stated, and one of the platforms.

fix.description: One thing that is done to a copy so it runs under Stoker, or that a player can choose to have done: a patch, a mod, a language, the publisher's own setup. An ordered list of steps, applied together or not at all. Fixes are applied in order — a build's own first, then its release's, then its game's, each list in its order — and each fix's `when` is checked against the files as they are when its turn comes, so a fix written for an unpacked executable finds it unpacked.

id.description: Stable, so a release or a build can switch the fix off and a report can name it.

role.description: `setup`: the publisher's own install steps. `languagePack`: what a language needs. `dlc`: what a DLC needs. `unpacked`: the build's executables with a store's DRM wrapper removed — `unpack` steps only, which every instance carries out on its own copy and checks against the result recorded here. `patch`: a fix — a community patch, a publisher hotfix, a compatibility tweak. `mod`: content somebody added.

name.description: What a person reads in a list: "German", "Widescreen fix".

when.description: The copies the fix is for. Absent: every copy it is listed for. A fix whose `when` does not hold is not for this copy and is left out — which is how one fix written against an executable's bytes serves every copy, from every store or disk, that has those bytes.

appliedWhen.description: What shows the fix is already in place, so a copy somebody patched by hand is not patched twice.

optional.description: The copy works without it, so a player may leave it out. Not optional means applied whenever its `when` holds.

default.description: An optional fix, or one answering a question, that is chosen unless somebody says otherwise.

available.description: False for a fix that cannot produce a working install — kept, with its reason, so nobody offers it again. Assassin's Creed declares six languages, and Russian installs no executable.

enabled.description: False to keep the finding without applying it.

links.description: Where the fix is documented or comes from, for a person reading the entry.

gameFix.description: A fix listed on a game or a release rather than on one build: a patch or a mod for whichever copies its `when` holds for.

steps.description: Unpacking is a build's own `unpacked` fix, never a game's or a release's.

step.description: One thing a fix does. Most change the install once, when the fix is applied; `environment`, `arguments` and `windowsCompatibility` apply every time the game starts. A minor version adds kinds; a reader that meets one it does not know treats the build as needing a newer Stoker rather than leave the step out. `run`, `firewall`, `registry` and `environment` reach beyond the install's own files, so a contributor's step is held to the install (see each); only a step read from the publisher's own install script (`source`) may go further, because the publisher's installer would have done the same.

filesStep.description: Lay a set of files over the install; a path both have is replaced. The files are named by fingerprint — never stored here.

into.description: The folder they go into. Absent: the install root.

deleteStep.description: Remove files — an intro video that crashes, a launcher stub that must not run. A path that is not there is not an error.

iniSetStep.description: Set one key of an INI-style file, creating the file, section and key when they are missing and keeping everything else as it was.

hexEditStep.description: Change bytes of one file in place — the shape most widescreen and FOV fixes are published in. Each edit checks the bytes it replaces and refuses a file that has others there; the fix's `when` says which file, by hash, the offsets are for.

from.description: The bytes found there, lowercase hex.

to.description: The bytes written, lowercase hex; as many as `from`.

binaryPatchStep.description: Turn one file into another with a binary diff. The diff is named by hash, never stored here.

fromBlake3.description: The file before; any other is refused.

toBlake3.description: The file after; a result that hashes otherwise is discarded.

unpackStep.description: Remove a store's DRM wrapper (SteamStub and its kind) from one executable with an unpacker plugin, on the instance's own copy — the unpacked file is never in the repository, and neither is the unpacker. The result has to hash as recorded, or it is discarded and the fix fails: an unpacker that produced something else produced something nobody checked.

unpacker.description: The unpacker plugin, from the plugin catalogue, and its version: a different version may unpack to different bytes.

fromBlake3.description: The wrapped executable; any other is refused.

installScriptSource.description: The install script (one of the build's `installScripts`) a step was read from. Absent for a step a contributor added.

registryStep.description: Write one registry value. Windows only. A contributor's step writes only below the game's own key — `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\<vendor>\…` or `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\<vendor>\…` (`WOW6432Node` allowed), never under `Microsoft`, `Classes`, `Policies`, `RegisteredApplications` or `Clients`, which is where autostarts, file associations and policy live. A step read from an install script (`source`) writes what the publisher's installer would have.

key.description: The full key, hive included, spelt out: `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Publisher\Game`.

language.description: The language the value is written for; absent for every language.

enabled.description: False to keep a step read from a script without carrying it out.

firewallStep.description: Let one program through Windows Firewall. Windows only. A contributor's step names a program inside the install; only a step read from an install script (`source`) may name one elsewhere.

name.description: The rule's name, which Windows shows in its list.

runStep.description: Run a program once the files are in place (`run`) or before they are removed (`runOnUninstall`): the publisher's own setup step, or a fix's patcher. Off by default for an `.exe` with no switches, which would put a UI in front of the player. A contributor's step runs a program inside the install — one a `files` step laid there, typically; only a step read from an install script (`source`) may run one elsewhere.

hasRunKey.description: Where Steam records having run it.

environmentStep.description: Set an environment variable every time the game starts. Not one that makes a runtime load code the variable names (`LD_PRELOAD`, `DYLD_*`, `COR_PROFILER`, `DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS`, `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` and their kind): code a fix needs goes into the install, where a hash says what it is.

mode.description: `set` replaces the variable. `prepend` and `append` add to a list such as `PATH`, joined with the machine's list separator (`;` on Windows, `:` elsewhere) — and simply set it when it is empty.

launch.description: Only for this launch. Absent: every launch.

argumentsStep.description: Add arguments to the command line every time the game starts, after the launch's own.

launch.description: Only for this launch. Absent: every launch.

windowsCompatibilityStep.description: Start one executable under Windows compatibility layers — `WINXPSP3`, `HIGHDPIAWARE`, `DISABLEDXMAXIMIZEDWINDOWEDMODE` — as the Compatibility tab would. Windows only.

hooks.description: Declarative export hooks for Stoker's bootstrap. Written verbatim beside every patched bootstrap as `stoker_hooks.json`, whose parser refuses unknown fields — so this definition is as strict as that parser. `{ "hooks": [] }` explicitly disables hooks.

behavior.description: `return` skips the original; `forward` tail-calls it; `intercept` calls it and observes the result.

value.description: Signed 32-bit forced or override result; sign-extended on x64.

override.description: Intercept only: substitute `value` for the result.

param.description: 1-based index of a string argument to rewrite; 0 disables rewriting.

wide.description: The string is UTF-16 rather than narrow ASCII.

when.description: Guards on arguments' low 32 bits; all must match before the string is read.
